title: Katseye’s Sophia to Sit Out European Leg of ‘Wildworld’ Tour to ‘Focus on Her Well-Being’
description: Katseye member Sophia Laforteza will not be joining the group for the U.K. and European dates of their upcoming “Wildworld” tour, which is scheduled
body:
Katseye member Sophia Laforteza will not be joining the group for the U.K. and European dates of their upcoming “Wildworld” tour, which is scheduled to launch on Tuesday.

	In a statement posted to social media, Katseye‘s label said that Laforteza is committed to “focusing on her well-being” after announcing her temporary hiatus from the group in early August. “The company remains fully committed to providing her with all the support and resources needed,” reads the statement. “Sophia will not be participating in THE WILDWORLD TOUR in Europe and the UK scheduled from September 1 through September 17.”
	

	The message continues, “We sincerely ask for EYEKONS’ warm understanding, as our highest priority will always be the health and long-term well-being of our artists. We will share further updates as they become available. Please continue to send your love, warmth, and support to Sophia and KATSEYE.”


	This marks yet another wrinkle for Katseye, which has had a series of swings throughout the year. In February, just after they performed at the Grammys, member Manon Bannerman announced that she would be taking a temporary hiatus from Katseye to “focus on her health and wellbeing.” Earlier this month, Laforteza announced that she would be following suit so that she could prioritize her “mental health and wellness.” Then, just days before Olivia Rodrigo’s Daisy Chain Fields Festival, where they were slated to perform, the group dropped out of the lineup, citing member Megan Skiendiel’s ankle injury as the reason for their absence.

	Amid it all, Katseye has continued to soar as a pop force, earning their first No. 1 album on the Billboard 200 with “Wild” in August. The “Wildworld” tour is slated to kick off on Tuesday at Dublin’s 3Arena, with stops planned for Paris, Amsterdam and Copenhagen. Katseye will head back to the States for an extensive leg in North America beginning on October 13 at Miami’s Kaseya Center.

schema.headline: Katseye’s Sophia to Sit Out European Leg of ‘Wildworld’ Tour to ‘Focus on Her Well-Being’

title: Enhypen Lands First No. 1, Dolly Parton Reenters Top Five on Albums Chart
description: Enhypen has scored its first No. 1 on the Billboard 200 with “The Sin : Bliss,” while Dolly Parton reentered the top 5 with “Ultimate Dolly Parton”
body:
Enhypen has scored its first No. 1 on the Billboard 200 with “The Sin : Bliss,” while Dolly Parton reentered the top 5 with “Ultimate Dolly Parton” following news of her death earlier this week.

	K-pop group Enhypen moved 98,000 equivalent album units in their first week with “The Sin : Bliss,” marking their seventh top 10 over the past four years. Enhypen previously reached No. 2 on the albums chart with “The Sin : Vanish” earlier this year, and also reached the same position with 2024’s “Romance : Untold.”
	

	Additionally, Parton returned to the top 10 with “Ultimate Dolly Parton,” which re-entered the chart at No. 5 with 59,000 equivalent album units. The country icon released the greatest hits collection in 2003 and peaked at No. 112 in 2019. With the resurgence of “Ultimate Dolly Parton,” the singer notches her fourth top 10 and her second-highest-charting album ever.


	Parton, who died at 80 after a short battle with cancer, saw a sharp increase in streams following news of her death. On Spotify, total streams increased over 1,260% globally and 2,320% in the United States in the first 24 hours after her death was announced. “Jolene” had the biggest surge with 630% globally and 1,225% in the U.S., while “9 to 5” increased 620% globally and 1,030% in the U.S. and “Islands in the Stream” increased 525% globally and 1,235% in the U.S.

	Elsewhere in the top 10, Ella Langley’s “Dandelion” lands at No. 2 followed by Olivia Rodrigo’s “You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love” at No. 3 and Morgan Wallen’s “I’m the Problem” at No. 4. Rounding out Nos. 6 through 10 are Katseye’s “Wild,” Noah Kahan’s “The Great Divide,” Stray Kids’ “This & That,” Drake’s “Iceman” and Ariana Grande’s “Petal.”

schema.headline: Enhypen Lands First No. 1, Dolly Parton Reenters Top Five on Albums Chart

title: Sandra Bullock Seemingly Drops Hint That Olivia Rodrigo and Stevie Nicks Have Music in ‘Practical Magic 2’
description:
Will Olivia Rodrigo and Stevie Nicks bring their musical talents to “Practical Magic 2?”

	Star Sandra Bullock seemed to teased the two pop stars’ i
body:
Will Olivia Rodrigo and Stevie Nicks bring their musical talents to “Practical Magic 2?”

	Star Sandra Bullock seemed to teased the two pop stars’ involvement in the Warner Bros. sequel in a post on her Instagram Story Sunday morning. Along with a video of Rodrigo and Nicks performing together, Bullock wrote, “Angel voices that are part of an upcoming film….”



	

	



	Reps for Nicks, Rodrigo and Warner Bros. did not immediately respond to Variety’s request for comment.
	

	Nicks had two songs in the original “Practical Magic,” both produced by Sheryl Crow.  


	During Saturday’s Daisy Chain Fields music festival, Rodrigo brought out Nicks to perform the 1975 Fleetwood Mac classic “Landslide.” “She reminds me of me, when I was her age a hundred years ago,” Nicks said of Rodrigo after taking the stage. “And I’m somewhat awestruck that she could do all this. Because it’s so hard, you have no idea, putting this together with all of these people. And she’s done it, with this grace.”

	“Practical Magic 2,” which sees the return of original star Nicole Kidman alongside Bullock, hits theaters on Sept. 11. Directed by “Bird Box” filmmaker Susanne Bier, the fantasy drama follows Bullock’s Sally, Kidman’s Gillian and their family of witches as they attempt to break a curse that has haunted them for generations. Other cast members include Stockard Channing, Dianne Wiest, Cassie Bradley, Joey King, Maisie Williams and Lee Pace. Akiva Goldsman, Georgia Pritchett and Kelly Marcel penned the script.

	The original “Practical Magic” hit theaters in 1998 to lukewarm reception. However, the film grew a cult following once it came to home video. “Practical Magic 2” is just the latest product of the Y2K nostalgia rush taking over Hollywood. 2026 brought “The Devil Wears Prada 2,” “Scary Movie” and “Toy Story 5” to theaters, while 2027 has “Shrek 5” and Greta Gerwig’s “Narnia” film slated for release.

schema.headline: Sandra Bullock Seemingly Drops Hint That Olivia Rodrigo and Stevie Nicks Have Music in ‘Practical Magic 2’

title: ‘Days of Thunder’ Star Randy Quaid Says Anne Hathaway Is ‘Woke’ and a ‘Horrible Choice’ for the Sequel: ‘You Need the Original Girl’
description: “Days of Thunder” star Randy Quaid sounded off on Anne Hathaway after it was revealed that she has joined Tom Cruise in the racing drama’s upcoming
body:
“Days of Thunder” star Randy Quaid sounded off on Anne Hathaway after it was revealed that she has joined Tom Cruise in the racing drama’s upcoming sequel.

	“We need Nicole [Kidman] back,” Quaid wrote on X Saturday. “Don’t be a pussy, [Tom Cruise]. You need the original girl. It’s not personal; it’s filmmaking. Anne isn’t sexy, because and if you haven’t noticed, she’s pregnant.”


	He added in a follow-up post, “Anne Hathaway is a leftist, woke, horrible choice for ‘DAYS OF THUNDER’ NASCAR audience who are MAGA. The sexy older chick for Tom in this film needs to be Nicole. That’s the casting that would sell the idea. It’s interesting because when we made the first one there was also a rush to get it out; editors slept in the cutting room on shifts. This is a weird thing, like they want it to come out and tank.”
	

	Reps for Paramount and Hathaway did not immediately respond to Variety’s request for comment.

	In the original “Days of Thunder,” Quaid played Tim Daland, the owner of the racing team that recruits Cruise’s up-and-coming driver Cole Trickle. As noted by Quaid, Nicole Kidman played Dr. Claire Lewicki, the romantic lead in the film. Other cast members include Robert Duvall, Cary Elwes and John C. Reilly. Tony Scott served as director.

	Variety exclusively reported Hathaway’s involvement in the “Days of Thunder” sequel. Paramount has slated the film for a June 2028 theatrical release. The project was shot for Imax and will hit screens nearly 40 years after the original.

schema.headline: ‘Days of Thunder’ Star Randy Quaid Says Anne Hathaway Is ‘Woke’ and a ‘Horrible Choice’ for the Sequel: ‘You Need the Original Girl’

title: President Trump Calls For FCC Punishment of NBC News’ Kristen Welker Following Promotional ‘Meet the Press’ Banter
description: President Donald Trump suggested referring NBC News anchor Kristen Welker for possible punishment by the Federal Communications Commission after the
body:
President Donald Trump suggested referring NBC News anchor Kristen Welker for possible punishment by the Federal Communications Commission after the “Meet the Press” moderator made innocuous remarks about candidates the President has backed in the run-up to the nation’s midterm elections later this year.

	Trump’s chilling diatribe, released via Truth Social, appeared to be misinformed. During a local segment in which Welker previewed her program with anchors on NBC’s Washington, D.C. station, WRC, she said that Trump had enjoyed “mixed results,” with some of the Republican candidates he’s backed losing in primaries, but also noted that Trump is “going to loom large over these midterms. There’s no doubt about that.”
	

	Trump called for Welker to be  “reported to the FCC for rebuke or punishment.” The Commission can’t directly mete out condemnation to individual journalists, but it can put bumps in the path of the company that owns the station as well as NBC News. That would be NBCUniversal, currently a unit of Comcast that is slated to be spun off from its parent over the next several months.


	“Kristen is one of the best in the business and we stand by her,” NBC News said in a statement Sunday afternoon. Welker did not utter any of the remarks that angered Trump during NBC’s actual broadcast of “Meet the Press” on Sunday.

	Under Trump and Chairman Brendan Carr, the FCC has been more activist than at any other time in recent memory. The Commission is currently enmeshed in a legal tangle with Walt Disney Co and ABC. The FCC has ordered Disney to file for renewals for ABC’s eight owned-and-operated stations years ahead of schedule. In filings, Disney has said its applications were made “under protest in response to an unlawful, arbitrary, and unconstitutional order.” “The View,” which has thrived in recent years with discussion of politics, has also found itself in the administration’s crosshairs. The FCC has probed whether the program has violated so-called “equal-time” election laws following the appearance of political figures, launching its investigation after James Talarico, the Democratic Senate candidate from Texas, appeared on the show in February. The FCC issued new guidance in January that late-night and daytime hosts needed to give equal time to political candidates from various parties, claiming the programs might be working along partisan lines.
	

	Disney and ABC have alleged in a suit filed in U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia that the FCC is in violation of the First Amendment.

	Trump’s relationship with Welker appears to run hot and cold. Many of the interviews he agrees to do with NBC News have been with her, and Trump has made a handful of appearances on “Meet the Press” to speak with her. But on Sunday, he called Welker “the Unpopular ‘Hostess’ of the once great Meet the Press, now considered Meet the Fake Press.”

	To be sure, Welker’s analysis was accurate. Some candidates backed by Trump, including Randy Feenstra, a Republican candidate for the Iowa governor seat, and Mike Lindell, the MyPillow CEO who made a bid to run as the Republican candidate in Minnesota’s gubernatorial race, both lost in primaries. More recently, Senator Darline Graham, who has filled in on an interim basis for her late brother, former South Carolina Senator Lindsey Graham, won a primary for the Senate seat in her home state.

schema.headline: President Trump Calls For FCC Punishment of NBC News’ Kristen Welker Following Promotional ‘Meet the Press’ Banter

title: Box Office: ‘The Dog Stars’ Bombs With $8 Million; ‘Spider-Man’ Continues Reign in Fifth Weekend
description:
“The Dog Stars” couldn’t beat the heat during the dog days of summer and melted down over its opening weekend.

	Disney and 20th Century’s “The Dog
body:
“The Dog Stars” couldn’t beat the heat during the dog days of summer and melted down over its opening weekend.

	Disney and 20th Century’s “The Dog Stars” opened to just $8 million domestically from 3,330 locations for a fifth-place finish. The post-apocalyptic thriller, which cost more than $80 million to produce, has not sat well with critics or audiences, receiving a 40% on Rotten Tomatoes and just a “C+” grade from CinemaScore polls.
	

	“The Dog Stars” is poised to lose tens of millions in its theatrical run, making it one of director Ridley Scott’s biggest misfires. The poor opening harkens back to Scott’s 2021 film “The Last Duel,” which opened to just $4.7 million in October of that year against a budget of about $100 million. The historical drama was also released by 20th Century, but it was received much better by critics. Scott, best known for classics like “Gladiator” and “Alien,” reached his box office peak in 2015 with “The Martian,” which grossed $630 million worldwide and earned seven Oscar nominations, including best picture. 


	“The Dog Stars” brings an up-and-down summer to an end for Disney. While the studio hit big with “Toy Story 5” ($1.12 billion) and “The Devil Wears Prada 2” ($692 million), it also fielded misfires like the live-action “Moana” ($308 million against a $250 million budget) and “The Mandalorian and Grogu” ($345 million against a $165 million budget). Hard to imagine Disney is worried, considering “Avengers: Doomsday” is waiting in the wings for what will surely be a box office blowout in December.
	

	“The Dog Star” stars Jacob Elordi as Hig, a lonely apocalypse survivor with a canine companion. After he picks up on a mysterious broadcast signal, he is determined to track the source. Other cast members include Margaret Qualley, Josh Brolin, Guy Pearce, Allison Janney and Benedict Wong.

	This weekend’s other major newcomer, “Coyote vs. Acme,” landed in third place after grossing an estimated $13.5 million domestically from 3,575 screens. The live-action-animation hybrid was abandoned by its original distributor, Warner Bros., for tax credits, enraging sectors of the film community. Ketchup Entertainment saved the title back in March of 2025 and slated it for a theatrical release.

	“Coyote vs. Acme” sees “Looney Tunes” favorite Wile E. Coyote take the Acme Corporation to court after its products failed him one too many times in his pursuit of the Road Runner. Cast members include Will Forte, Lana Condor, John Cena, Tone Bell, Martha Kelly, Luis Guzmán, P.J. Byrne and John Early. Dave Green directs with a script from Samy Burch.

	At No. 1, again, was Sony and Marvel’s “Spider-Man: Brand New Day.” It earned $22.2 million through Sunday, dropping just 44% from last week’s earnings. That figure pushes the superhero epic’s domestic total to a staggering $891 million.

	“Brand-New Day” is on the cusp of two major box office milestones. After surpassing $936 million, it will become the highest-grossing movie of all time at the domestic box office. That record currently belongs to 2015’s “Star Wars: The Force Awakens.” When it clears that benchmark, “Spider-Man” will be on its way to becoming the first movie ever to hit $1 billion in North America alone. 

	Universal’s “The Odyssey” continues to impress. The Greek epic took second, earning $14.6 million through its seventh weekend at the domestic box office. That puts Chris Nolan’s blockbuster at a North American haul of $564 million.

	Sony’s “Insidious: Out of the Further” made $10.1 million (a 60% drop) in its second weekend for a fourth-place finish. Those earnings put the horror sequel’s domestic revenues at $43 million. It’s a great start, considering the film only cost about $18 million to produce.

schema.headline: Box Office: ‘The Dog Stars’ Bombs With $8 Million; ‘Spider-Man’ Continues Reign in Fifth Weekend

title: ‘Call My Agent! The Movie’ Review: Love-Hate Energy Keeps the Gang Together in a Fast, Funny Feature-Length Return
description: The rare reboot pitch that that can actually be greeted with “this again!” rather than “this again?,” “Call My Agent! The Movie” makes sense of its
body:
The rare reboot pitch that that can actually be greeted with “this again!” rather than “this again?,” “Call My Agent! The Movie” makes sense of its rote title in two ways. First, and most obviously, it’s a feature-length spinoff of the hit French comedy series, which wittily satirized the national showbiz industry from the perspective of its beleaguered talent agents. But second, “the movie” doesn’t just refer to the one we’re watching, as this two-hour return tracks the tortured production process of the first film directed by the show’s heroine, now-former agent Andréa Martel (Camille Cottin). But if the point of view has changed, the comedy remains on-target: Fleet and fast-talking and packed, as ever, with Gallic industry in-jokes and celebrity cameos, Émilie Noblet’s film can hardly fail to please longtime fans when it hits Netflix on Sept. 10.
	

	Nearly six years have passed since the fourth season of “Call My Agent!” concluded on something of a bombshell — as the Paris-based talent agency Agence Samuel Kerry (ASK) folded in a state of near-bankruptcy, with its employees scattered in various ambiguous directions. If not altogether unhappy, it was a destabilizing ending that hit pretty hard when the final episode hit in late 2020, given that COVID at that point had the global entertainment industry in a state of crippling uncertainty. So it’s comforting to see the old faces of ASK back with new career trajectories, even if — as fey former assistant Hervé (Nicolas Maury) makes clear in a catch-up intro delivered directly to camera — some are doing better than others.
	

	Doing very well for themselves indeed are former ASK hotshot Mathias (Thibault de Montalembert), still representing A-list talent at the new agency he founded with his daughter Camille (Fanny Sidney), and his erstwhile assistant turned wife Noémie (Laure Calamy), who has found surprising success as a TV producer. His old office rival Andréa, meanwhile, is happy to have left agenting behind for a more creative career as a writer-director, though as her debut feature “The Fugitive” (not a remake of the Harrison Ford vehicle) enters pre-production, she despairs to find herself putting out fires all too familiar from her former line of work. 

	It doesn’t help that her intended leading man Laurent Lafitte (popping up very drolly as himself) is represented by Mathias, still nursing professional grudges and willing to sabotage the whole project — even when Noémie jumps on board as producer. Andréa’s first choice for that job, Eva Longoria, smilingly puts herself out of contention when she suggests that the script, a gritty female survivalist revenge drama led by Laetitia Casta, might work better as a Parisian wish-fulfilment romance. 

	Americans in general are not helpful allies on this enterprise: Wes Anderson doesn’t appear on screen, but his latest shoot scuppers proceedings from afar, while in a standout cringe-comedy scene, an initially encouraging meeting with George Clooney (another good-humored cameo) goes south when  Noémie inadvertently disses his direction of the mediocre WWII romp “The Monuments Men.” The script, by showrunner Fanny Herrero with Lison Daniel, tosses out throwaway barbs so pacily and plentifully that industry outsiders may not altogether keep up with the satire — though it’s hard to miss Gérard Depardieu catching some well-earned strays. 

	Just as often, however, the characters reserve their ire for each other: Though the gang is now scattered, the film still captures the fizzy love-hate relations that made the series such a winning workplace comedy. “Call My Agent! The Movie” will play amusingly enough for non-acolytes, but it does assume some knowledge of the show’s tangled character dynamics. Drawing a slightly short straw in this story is Andréa’s estranged best friend Gabriel (Grégory Montel), now unhappily working at rival agency Starmédia, though it speaks to the show’s relative complexity that a movie-length reboot can’t tie up all loose ends — even if a calamitous turn in Andréa’s shoot winds up uniting nearly everyone toward a common cause.
	

	Though it’s slickly cut and shot in surprisingly glossy widescreen by gifted DP Aurélien Marra (an ASC winner a few years back for “Two of Us”), the greatest pleasures of the film are the more televisual ones of the original series: the breathless cut and thrust of the dialogue, and the immaculate timing of the performances. Cottin remains a drily smart, likably peppery lead, perfectly countering the spiraling scattiness of the wonderful Calamy. They’re a double act to treasure here, their passive-aggressive exchanges the stuff of sitcom perfection, and plenty pleasurable in movie form too.

schema.headline: ‘Call My Agent! The Movie’ Review: Love-Hate Energy Keeps the Gang Together in a Fast, Funny Feature-Length Return

title: Olivia Rodrigo Raises $20 Million With Daisy Chain Fields Festival Thanks to Matching Commitment From Melinda French Gates
description: Olivia Rodrigo raised a significant sum of $10 million with her inaugural Daisy Chain Fields Festival — and then doubled it to $20 million, thanks t
body:
Olivia Rodrigo raised a significant sum of $10 million with her inaugural Daisy Chain Fields Festival — and then doubled it to $20 million, thanks to a matching commitment from philanthropist Melinda French Gates.

	Rodrigo introduced her own headlining set at the festival on Saturday in Irvine, California by thanking the crowd for attending and revealing that the event, which featured a robust lineup including Rodrigo, Chappell Roan, Doechii, Garbage and more, had raised $10 million. She then revealed that Gates had contributed another $10 million, bringing the overall sum to $20 million.
	

	“Daisy Chain Fields is about what can happen when we come together and use our collective power to support one another,” said Rodrigo. “I’m incredibly grateful to Melinda and Pivotal for believing in this mission and making the impact of our first festival twice as powerful. Most of all, I’m so excited about what this means for the incredible organizations we’re supporting and the women, girls and communities they show up for every single day.”


	Gates joined Rodrigo on stage to commend her for her philanthropic efforts with Daisy Chain Fields. “Olivia Rodrigo is a force,” said French Gates. “What Daisy Chain Fields sets in motion will last far beyond a single night, by opening up opportunity for women and girls around the world and showing a new generation how much their voices matter. I’m so proud to support Olivia’s vision.”

	The $20 million will be distributed equally across 10 different nonprofit organizations supporting women and girls. Among the organizations are Baby2Baby, Black Mamas Matter Alliance, Center for Reproductive Rights, FreeForm, Jhpiego, Johns Hopkins Center for Indigenous Health, National Domestic Workers Alliance, National Institute for Reproductive Health, National Women’s Law Center and Planned Parenthood.
	

	At the festival, attendees enjoyed performances from a slew of performers that also included Bikini Kill, Eli, Mitski, Not for Radio, Rachel Chinouriri, Santigold, the Breeders and more. Throughout the day, concertgoers were encouraged to learn about the nonprofits through Daisy Chain Reaction, which offered information about the causes.

schema.headline: Olivia Rodrigo Raises $20 Million With Daisy Chain Fields Festival Thanks to Matching Commitment From Melinda French Gates

title: At Daisy Chain Fields, Olivia Rodrigo, Chappell Roan and Honored Forebears Convene for a Superb Festival That’s Hot to Go in Every Way: Concert Review
description: You know an inaugural festival has been a success when, after the temperature reached 95 degrees, humidity topped 80%… perspiration stains were so p
body:
You know an inaugural festival has been a success when, after the temperature reached 95 degrees, humidity topped 80%… perspiration stains were so pervasive that it was the odd dry spots that looked like stains… constant 12-minute trudges back and forth between two action-packed stages threatened to sap what few excess pounds hadn’t been sweated off… and you realized that, amid those conditions, you had not sat down in more than 10 hours… and, sitting in a gridlocked lot waiting to get out, all you could think was:
	

	How soon do we get to do this again?


	The answer to that, at the end of the Daisy Chain Fields festival Saturday in Irvine, Calif., was some time around this year in 2027. Festival creator and headliner Olivia Rodrigo told the 45,000-strong crowd the words they wanted to hear: that this was not a one-off, and that we’d reconvene next year for another thrillingly curated, expertly executed and altogether spirit-rewarding all-female-led bill. (Flowery adjectives ours, not hers.)

	Now if they could just find a way to schedule future editions of the festival at a more meteorologically reasonable time, some period of the year where it is reliably warm in SoCal yet not prone to insanely long heat waves, because climate change has abated and… well, never mind, fine … August probably is as good a time as any.

	What a distraction from all that the 14-act bill (plus three guest stars) managed to provide over a 10-and-a-half-hour day of music, with one killer act after another representing a wide gamut of styles and eras, bearing a sold amount of diversity except for the lone common-denominator criterion for booking. 
	


	Of course it ended with Sarah McLachlan, the instigator of the obvious inspiration, Lilith Fair, taking the stage to implicitly give her blessing for carrying on the tradition, as she joined Rodrigo’s stage for duets of “Building a Mystery” and “Angel” (the latter dedicated to Dolly Parton, with permission given to cry, because McLachlan knows she’s good at that). Or not literally quite the end, actually, because it was inevitable when Stevie Nicks was announced as one of Rodrigo’s guests that you don’t follow that.



	

					Olivia Rodrigo and Sarah McLachlan at Daisy Chain Fields Festival 2026 held at Great Park on August 29, 2026 in Irvine, California.
									Christopher Polk
	




	As an ambassador from the 1970s, Nicks was an outlier in this company, where nearly all of the acts were either fairly newly minted stars or heroines of the Lilith era. There was a case being made here, without stating it quite so bluntly, that the two greatest decades for women in pop music were the ’90s and the 2020s. History isn’t quite that simple, but for 10-plus hours Saturday, I was ready to jump in and readily make the case that the respective eras of Alanis Morissette (who also showed up as a surprise guest) and Rodrigo really were and are the greatest generations, whether it can be empirically backed up or not.

	At the very least, the two climactic main stage sets, by Rodrigo and Chappell Roan, set out a pretty indisputable case that we are living in a golden era. Between the two of them, they are responsible for four of the dozen greatest albums of the decade (i.e., Roan’s lone effort so far and all three of Rodrigo’s, peaking with her best achievement to date, “You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love”). It would have been lovely to see them share a moment on stage together, and we didn’t get that. But it was enough to have them performing superb sets back to back in an effective coronation and celebration of these two as the greatest pop figures currently in their 20s.



	

					Chappell Roan at Daisy Chain Fields Festival 2026 held at Great Park on August 29, 2026 in Irvine, California.
									Christopher Polk
	



	But if you were looking for the secret heart of the festival, it might have been over on the second stage, where some of the artists who inspired Rodrigo as a nascent rocker got their moment to shine. It would be hard to imagine a more heartwarming moment than when Bikini Kill revved through some vintage punk and the entire crowd of young ‘uns in front was singing along. Kathleen Hanna was at least as agog as any of the rest of us at the realization the band was playing to a pretty full and definitely engaged field of (primarily) women, something that would have seemed like science-fiction in their heyday. Hanna said that when they played Orange County in the ’90s, they were lucky if three women showed up to one of their gigs (and then she brought out three Irvine-ites who did form their own band after getting into Bikini Kill). Not all good things come to those who wait, but occasionally poetic justice prevails.
	



	

					Shirley Manson of Garbage performs onstage at Daisy Chain Fields Festival 2026 held at Great Park on August 29, 2026 in Irvine, California.
									Gilbert Flores
	



	The Breeders and Garbage kept the ’90s magic happening on the Marigold Stage, where, in the afternoon and late evening heat, everyone would have been very happy if Shirley Manson had actually been able to summon rain. Kim Deal and company were confident enough to put “Cannonball” right in the middle of their set and not save it for the end; they also provided the day’s sole quotient of country music, with vintage C&W homage “Drivin’ on 9.” Manson was as un-shy as ever when it came to passionate monologs between songs, speaking about how the band wrote songs about LGBTQ+ themes before they or the culture had discovered the language that now exists. But those songs hardly suffered for not yet having a common terminology to reference.



	

					The Breeders at Daisy Chain Fields Festival 2026 held at Great Park on August 29, 2026 in Irvine, California.
									Christopher Polk
	



	A danger in doing a festival like this is that 90% of the crowd may claim their spots in the main field — for the Dandelion Stage, as it was known here — and never budge for fear of losing their spots. So it was a pleasure to see (if not always so much to participate in) the mass migration that occurred between those two spaces every 30 or 40 minutes, and to see how many twentysomethings and even teens wanted to see the legends of ’90s women in rock. That stage was not strictly themed, though; the final act of the night over yonder was Not for Radio, the band formed by Marias singer Maria Zardoya, whose very chill style for this side project was perfectly timed for a post-dusk time slot, whereas it might’ve been too ambient for comfort in the heat of the day.



	

					Maria Zardoya of Not for Radio at Daisy Chain Fields Festival 2026 held at Great Park on August 29, 2026 in Irvine, California.
									Gilbert Flores
	



	Back at the larger field, there could hardly have been a greater study in contrasts than seeing Mitski followed by Doechii, even if their mononym names feel phonetically compatible, and even if there was a shared excellence uniting them. Mitski was one of those acts who really would be better suited for a nighttime slot, but she was in her most energetic, stage-traversing mode, and ending on the greatest cat-lady anthem of all time, “That White Cat,” allowed for a ferocious finale. There were a lot of passionate female-forward statements made during the day, as is natural, but Mitski is the kind of artist who really represents women (and people) in all their complications; some of the songs she performed were about pure, unabated need, bordering on self-abasement at times… yet her stage persona is so powerful that you feel quite confident you’d come out on the wrong end if you ever really crossed her.
	



	

					Mitski at Daisy Chain Fields Festival 2026 held at Great Park on August 29, 2026 in Irvine, California.
									Christopher Polk
	




	Doechii had the strongest and most delightfully outrageous look of the day (rivaled only by Roan’s attention-getting makeover). She and her four dancers appeared with body makeup that put them in various shades of red and pink — kind of like a flow chart as to how some in the audience might have been changing color as the day went on. Doechii was of a different ilk than most everyone else on the bill in terms of being the kind of artist who brings tracks, not a band. That said, she was very much in competition for the title of greatest show-woman of the day, on top of offering flavors that otherwise might’ve been severely missed in a more purely pop-rock-driven lineup. (Complaining about the heat, she asked “Irvine” if it was always like this, then noted that she’s from Florida, which might have helped explain why she didn’t sweat off all that crimson.)



	

					Doechii performs onstage at Daisy Chain Fields Festival 2026 held at Great Park on August 29, 2026 in Irvine, California.
									Gilbert Flores
	



	Roan was all about the purple, shocking the audience with a head-to-toe different look that had her dressed in an outfit that looked like someone’s fever dream of what a TWA stewardess uniform should have looked like in the ’60s. Her hair is still red, but now straightened and shortened into a bob; the curly and queenly aura is now history in favor of something that is even h-o-t-t-e-r-t-o-go. Whether it had to do with the outfit or just where she’s at in between tours, Roan seemed more energized and physically on-point than she ever has on stage — including some high kicks that could make a Rockette jealous — while also effortlessly mastering the demands of a “Good Luck, Babe” and other vocally challenging numbers. There were no surprises in her 40-minute set; “Only the hits today. It’s only the hits,” she warned the audience. But a new stylistic outlook did as much work as a new song might’ve, in helping keep an audience transfixed as she steamed through highlights of the greatest single-album catalog anyone has managed lately. 




	

					Chappell Roan at Daisy Chain Fields Festival 2026 held at Great Park on August 29, 2026 in Irvine, California.
									Christopher Polk
	



	At an hour and 20 minutes, Rodrigo’s closing set was 40 minutes longer than anyone else’s, having less to do with the generous amounts of “You Seem Pretty Sad…” appearing in a set of hers for the first time than space built in for three guests stars. It was a nice touch that her guests were announced from the outset, rather than being held back as a surprise, allowing for their inclusion on the T-shirts, etc. That turned out to be a premature move, after all, when Karen O had to cancel her cameo because of an emergency, Rodrigo told the crowd. There was still a third guest, though, as the day’s one true surprise, Morissette, came aboard for an “Ironic” duet. Rodrigo-as-natural-pro came to the forefront here as her voice proved an easy and flawless harmonic complement to Alanis on that number, and to McLachlan on “Mystery” and “Angel,” and to Nicks on the closing “Landslide.” 
	




	

					Olivia Rodrigo and Melinda Gates speak onstage at Daisy Chain Fields Festival 2026 held at Great Park on August 29, 2026 in Irvine, California.
									Gilbert Flores
	



	Rodrigo’s set was preceded by the star bringing out Melinda French Gates to announce that the philanthropist was matching the $10 million already announced by Rodrigo as going toward the 10 charity beneficiaries with a dollar-for-dollar additional $10 million. Rodrigo does not require much to put an additional spring in her step, but her giddiness was at its peak, maybe not least of all because of having a successful and (most importantly of all) non-catastrophic first festival outing being extra wind beneath her rocker-girl wings. It’s hard to tell just how much of a preview this was or wasn’t of the tour that kicks off in Hartford next month, but getting in seven of the 12 tracks from “You Seem Pretty Sad…” — basically, all but the saddest ones — plus the newly released non-album song “Serena Joy” felt more than justified. If anything, you might’ve had mixed feelings about hearing singles as tried and true as “Good 4 U,” only because of knowing still another “Pretty Sad” song could have gotten its live premiere in that slot. All of which is beating around the bush on the way to say that the set was pretty unassailable for an abridgement of what is about to come on tour.



	

					Chappell Roan at Daisy Chain Fields Festival 2026 held at Great Park on August 29, 2026 in Irvine, California.
									Christopher Polk
	



	With the show over, Nicks didn’t want to leave the stage, even after Rodrigo did, not because she had a second song to sing, but because she had the same instinct almost every performer did Saturday — to speak the younger artist’s praises for pulling this off. These were merited accolades. 

	Truth be told, there’ve been other all-female lineups since Lilith Fair went out with a whimper instead of a bang in its early 21st century revival: Brandi Carlile has long put on an all-female-headliner festival in Mexico every year, though the travel factor makes the bar to entry high. More subtly and slyly, the All Things Go festival that takes place each year in three eastern cities has become an almost all-female thing; you jave to love how the D.C. edition coming up next month has dozens of fantastic women on the bill… along with Father John Misty and Ryan Beatty as hilariously token dudes.
	

	But it takes a chart-topping superstar instigator to personally make phone calls for an annual event that will be an instant sellout, of the true FOMO variety, and — it feels like — an instant cultural touchstone. Even as Rodrigo’s and Nicks’ closing “Landslide” gave way to the landslide of 45,000 people trying to exit the gates, there was a communal bliss that not even one last Bataan march could spoil. Everyone seemed pretty elated for coming out of a festival that hadn’t toppled the patriarchy, but had proven again that, in 2026, women rule music in virtually every qualifiable way. In the Lilith Fair day, pushing women’s place in pop felt more aspirational; in 2026, as far as there is to go in other aspects of politics and culture, an event that puts them on top of the pops feels closer to a happy acknowledgement of what everyone already knows.

	And here’s one more thing we know: fans are going to have a lot of suggestions about who Rodrigo should call for year 2… And they can already start pre-complaining about the impossibility of getting tickets. Daisy Chain Fields tour, anyone?



	

					Olivia Rodrigo at Daisy Chain Fields Festival 2026 held at Great Park on August 29, 2026 in Irvine, California.
									Christopher Polk

schema.headline: At Daisy Chain Fields, Olivia Rodrigo, Chappell Roan and Honored Forebears Convene for a Superb Festival That’s Hot to Go in Every Way: Concert Review

title: 'Love & Hip Hop' Sidney Starr: Prosecutors Want to Keep Teen Accuser’s Sex History in Court

'Love & Hip Hop' Sidney Starr
                          Prosecutors Move to Block Teen Accuser’s
body:
'Love & Hip Hop' Sidney Starr
                          Prosecutors Move to Block Teen Accuser’s Sex History Out of Court
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              August 30, 2026
                            2:44 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            Sidney Starr is heading back to court this week in her child molestation case ... and prosecutors are already trying to limit what can be said about the alleged victim's sexual history.
      
    
            According to court docs obtained by TMZ, prosecutors filed a rape shield motion Thursday in the criminal case against the "Love & Hip Hop" alum.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            The motion asks the judge to keep the alleged victim's past sex life from being brought up in court, unless the law allows it.
      

            The filing comes just days after Sidney was denied bond and ordered to remain locked up while the charges are pending.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            As we reported ... Sidney was arrested Aug. 2 and charged with sodomy, aggravated child molestation and sexual battery against a child under 16.
      
    
            Police say Sidney met the male at an Embassy Suites in Hapeville and went back to her hotel room with him. Sidney told investigators he told her he was 18 ... while his parents told cops he was under 16.
      
    
            Sidney has denied the allegations and vowed to fight the case.
      
    
            Court records also show prosecutors filed a certificate of discovery and a notice of prosecution's intent Thursday.
      
    
            Sidney is due back in court this coming Thursday for her plea and arraignment.

title: Kanye West Exec Milo Yiannopoulos Breaks Silence After ICE Detention and Deportation
description:
Kanye West Exec Milo Yiannopoulos
                          Louisiana Can F*** Off!!!
body:
Kanye West Exec Milo Yiannopoulos
                          Louisiana Can F*** Off!!!
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              August 30, 2026
                            1:30 PM PDT
                                                                            
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Milo Yiannopoulos has broken his silence after getting booted from the U.S. ... and his first message from across the pond is a giant middle finger to Louisiana.
      
    
            Kanye West's former chief of staff surfaced on X Sunday, posting a screenshot of a KFC ad for a "Dirty Louisiana Burger" with the caption, "oh f*** off."
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            The timing is hard to miss ... Milo was detained by ICE in Louisiana Thursday before being deported back to the UK.
      

            TMZ broke the news ... Milo was taken into custody at the New Orleans airport over his immigration status and later transferred to an ICE detention center.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Federal officials said Milo legally entered the U.S. in 2019, but overstayed his authorized stay and was ultimately ordered to be deported after missing an immigration hearing in July.
      
    
            By Saturday, we also broke the news he was on his way back to Britain.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Milo was in New Orleans as Ye was in town for a Friday night concert ... and, as TMZ reported, Kanye and Bianca Censori were spotted leaving the city's airport not long after after Milo's trip through the same airport ended in ICE custody.
      
    
            Milo hasn't directly addressed the arrest or deportation yet ... but judging from his first post since getting the boot, Louisiana isn't exactly on his travel wish list.
